edges.description: Complete loss of Gcsh is embryonic lethal before mid-gestation and is not rescued by formate, consistent with an essential role beyond glycine cleavage.
edges.limitations: Human GCSH variants are hypomorphic and compatible with birth, whereas the mouse null dies before E10.5, so the model cannot show the postnatal NKH or lipoylation phenotypes; heterozygotes have normal plasma glycine.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic variants in GCSH encoding the moonlighting H-protein cause combined nonketotic hyperglycinemia and lipoate deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic variants in GCSH encoding the moonlighting H-protein cause combined nonketotic hyperglycinemia and lipoate deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Three patients (1,2,5) had a neonatal episode typical for NKH with coma, respiratory insufficiency, myoclonia and burst suppression on EEG.

nodes.description: Lipoyl-H-protein is the donor from which LIPT1 transfers lipoate to DLAT (PDH E2) and DLST (2-KGDH E2). Reduced or dysfunctional H-protein leaves these E2 subunits under-lipoylated.
nodes.id: Deficient Lipoylation of 2-Oxoacid Dehydrogenase E2 Subunits

evidence.reference_title: Protein moonlighting elucidates the essential human pathway catalyzing lipoic acid assembly on its cognate enzymes.
evidence.snippet: We report that the physiologically relevant LIPT1 enzyme activity is transfer of lipoyl moieties from the H protein of the glycine cleavage system to the E2 subunits of the 2-oxoacid dehydrogenases required for respiration

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic variants in GCSH encoding the moonlighting H-protein cause combined nonketotic hyperglycinemia and lipoate deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Here we report six new patients who presented with NKH and were found to carry bi-allelic variants in GCSH.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic variants in GCSH encoding the moonlighting H-protein cause combined nonketotic hyperglycinemia and lipoate deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic variants in GCSH encoding the moonlighting H-protein cause combined nonketotic hyperglycinemia and lipoate deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Although the lipoyl-H-protein amount was similar to controls, the lipoylated DLST levels and even DLAT levels did not recover, reflecting a decrease in lipoyl transfer

nodes.description: Biallelic GCSH variants (start-loss p.Met1?, splice, nonsense, exon deletion or duplication, and missense) reduce the amount or function of the H-protein. Most variants are hypomorphic and affect both of its roles; some missense variants affect mainly one.

nodes.description: Benzoate conjugates glycine to lower plasma glycine. In GCSH patients it restored breathing in one neonate and controlled spasms in another, but was stopped as ineffective in a third. The NKH GeneReviews chapter advises avoiding valproate, which raises glycine, and vigabatrin.
